newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's BCI makes overture to Cariplo.
newsitem.headline: Italy's BCI makes overture to Cariplo.

text.p: Banca Commerciale Italiana (BCI) has made an offer to take part in the privatisation of Italy's largest savings bank, Cassa di Risparmio delle Provincie Lombarde Cariplo, a BCI spokesman said on Sunday.
The spokesman gave no details of the offer but Italian newspapers said BCI's plan, if it came to fruition, would create a new leader in the Italian banking sector.
"An offer has been presented to Cariplo," the spokesman said, adding it would be examined by executives of the Foundation controlling Cariplo at a meeting due to take place on Monday.

Newspapers, citing sources at BCI, said the Milan-based bank wanted to take part in the expected privatisation of Cariplo by its controlling Foundation and form an all-round banking group which would be the largest in Italy in capital terms and the seventh or eighth biggest in Europe.
"The objective is to create a Milanese banking group of continental significance and entirely in Italian control," the daily Corriere della Sera said.
Newspapers said BCI had presented a three-pronged plan to the Cariplo Foundation, rivalling a proposal made by Banco Ambrosiano Veneto (Ambroveneto).
La Repubblica newspaper said BCI's first step would be to buy 25 to 30 percent of Cariplo's banking activities from the Foundation for around three trillion lire ($1.79 billion).
It would then put all its banking activities into a newly-formed holding company, which would also absorb the 70 percent of Cariplo bank still retained by the Foundation.
A third phase would include capital increases and the creation of shareholder syndicates giving the definitive form of the new banking group.

At the end of the operation the Cariplo Foundation would control 15 percent of the new holding company while BCI shareholders like insurer Generali, French bank Paribas and Germany's Commerzbank would control a further 15 percent.
The remaining 70 percent would be offered on the stock market for a total of more than five trillion lire, La Repubblica said.

Cariplo has said it hopes for a stock market flotation this year and Corriere said the Foundation's chairman, Giuseppe Guzzetti, wanted the sell-off on condition that there was an industrial plan strengthening Cariplo, that the sale generated cash and that the Foundation kept a joint role with its chosen ally.
Ambroveneto chairman Giovanni Bazoli said last month his bank was interested in a possible alliance with the savings bank but he first wanted to see its privatisation plans.
Italy's biggest bank, San Paolo di Torino, is currently in the process of being sold off by its controlling Foundation.

It begins a public share offer on Monday for nearly 27 percent of its capital, and the Foundation has already placed a further 20 percent in the hands of a stable core of institutional shareholders. ($1 = 1,672 lire)
